title: “More than medicine — but when?” A qualitative study of how general practitioners assess, negotiate, and apply social prescribing in clinical practice
Would it be worse to delay your product for seven days or for a week? How numerical framing influences company evaluations
abstract: Purpose Numerical information framing can influence consumer perceptions. Although numbers are present throughout the entire consumer journey, relatively little is known about how numerical information, such as unit framing, can influence consumer perceptions in the context of service failures. This research aims to investigate how differences in unit framing between contracted (e.g. a week) versus expanded (e.g. seven days) temporal units influence consumer perceptions and responses following time-based service failures. Design/methodology/approach The authors conduct three experiments testing the proposed hypotheses, process and boundary conditions. Findings This paper demonstrates that service failures using contracted temporal units can lead to less favorable company evaluations and reduce repurchase intentions. The authors propose that this happens because unit framing can influence company evaluations. They conclude by discussing implications for scholars and managers. Originality/value This work adds to the literature on unit framing and numerical cognition by showing how temporal unit framing can influence perceptions of service failures. The findings show that contracted temporal units can lead to worse outcomes after a service delay.

title: When AI talks politics: a critical look at Deontology and Utilitarianism in the age of synthetic campaign content
journal: Muallim Journal of Social Science and Humanities
abstract: Until very recently, when someone wanted some fabricated political content that appeared authentic, they needed a professional production team. Nowadays, anyone owning a computer is capable of doing it in merely several minutes. Artificial Intelligence makes people able to generate fake speeches. Thereby, this technology enables the generation of fake videos together with customized campaign ads appearing to be true ones. This raises an important ethical question for media ethics. This paper compares two well-known ethical theories to find out their respective views on such topic. They are Immanuel Kant’s deontology claiming people are obliged by virtue itself to follow certain moral imperatives no matter what situation people find oneself in (Kant, 1785). Another one is Utilitarianism proposed by John Stuart Mill which evaluates any deed according whether outcomes make most people feel satisfied and happy (Mill, 1861/ 2002). The paper takes up one actual example from the elections happened in Malaysia in April 2024 to find out how the above two kinds of ethical doctrines deal with that issue in reality. Someone utilized AI technology to reproduce the voice of one candidate, so everyone thought that the one had completely abandoned rural voters. As shown by the paper, there are different results when adopting deontology versus utilitarianism respectively. According to deontology, the individual has acted wrongly in any event no doubt about it. But for the viewpoint held by utilitarianism, it seems most probably he got something wrong but perhaps his behavior would gain legitimacy under some other conditions. Neither of them seems fully convincing alone when judged individually. Therefore, the conclusion presented by the paper here is a compromise between the two extremes called here Hybrid Framework which sticks to deontological principles but still admits utilitarian exceptions in case things happen in really serious cases. Finally, the conclusion section will give guidance and advice on relevant issues raised before to everyone in different walks including ordinary people, content creators and policymakers.

title: Ultrasound-targeted delivery of total extracts from Abelmoschus Manihot (L.) alleviates radiation-induced cardiomyocyte ferroptosis via the NOX4/SLC7A11/GPX4 axis
Towards sustainable public transit: development of representative driving cycles for electric and CNG buses using naturalistic micro-trip data from Patna, India
abstract: Abstract With the increasing emphasis on sustainable urban mobility, electric buses are rapidly being integrated into public transportation networks in Indian cities. A critical component in evaluating their energy consumption and operational efficiency is the development of representative driving cycles that reflect local driving conditions. This study presents a data-driven methodology to construct real-world driving cycles for electric and CNG buses operating on mixed urban and rural roads in Patna, India. High-frequency trajectory data, collected over a 1000 km stretch using VBOX GPS loggers, were segmented into micro-trips. The study proposed two methods, Modified Random Selection and k-means clustering, to identify representative segments for cycle construction. The resulting Patna Electric Bus Driving Cycle (PEBDC) and Patna CNG Bus Driving Cycle (PCBDC) are benchmarked against both Indian and international standards. It is observed that the Patna cycles exhibited lower average speeds and reduced time spent in acceleration and deceleration phases, when compared to driving cycles of other Indian cities.

The environment lens
journal: Development and Learning in Organizations: An International Journal
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings This paper identified that knowledge sharing whether implicit or explict can influence the innovation or mindfulness climates created within the organization. These climates can influence retention in many ways. Research limitations/implications The paper demonstrated the importance of the performance and emotional elements within the organization and how each can work to support business goals. Practical implications The paper highlighted how organizations should not just focus on a set of rules or guidelines but treat retention as a complex element that relies on several features. Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: Vision AI–Integrated 4D BIM for Real-Time Construction Progress Monitoring and Anomaly Detection
abstract: Construction progress monitoring and quality inspection in high-rise building projects are still largely dependent on manual processes, resulting in inefficient reporting, delayed decision-making, and inconsistent inspection quality. Existing studies generally focus on either Vision-AI-based progress monitoring or BIM-based schedule management, with limited integration of geometric anomaly detection into a unified framework. This study aims to develop and evaluate an integrated Vision-AI and 4D-BIM framework for automated construction progress monitoring and structural geometric anomaly detection. The proposed method combines transformer-based object detection, three-dimensional coordinate transformation, and 4D-BIM schedule synchronization to identify structural components, compare as-built conditions with BIM models, and monitor construction progress in real time. Experimental results demonstrated an average precision of 0.882, an average recall of 0.847, and an inference speed of 41.5 FPS, while successfully detecting structural deviations exceeding predefined tolerance limits and synchronizing construction progress with planned schedules. The novelty of this research lies in the integration of transformer-based Vision-AI, 4D-BIM synchronization, and automated geometric anomaly detection within a single computational framework capable of simultaneously performing progress monitoring and dimensional quality assessment. The proposed framework contributes to digital construction management by improving monitoring efficiency, reducing reliance on manual inspection, and supporting faster identification of schedule deviations and quality issues. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective and practical solution for intelligent construction monitoring in high-rise building projects.
